articles.body: Japanese domestic carrier Imoto Lines has deployed the newly built containership Minato on its western Japan service. The vessel was launched on 17 August and is owned by Fukuyoshi Kaiun. It was constructed by Koike Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering as the third vessel in the Maya class, following the delivery of the first ship in 2024. Although Imoto Lines describes Minato as a 200 TEU-class vessel, its stated maximum container capacity is 245 TEU, including space for 42 refrigerated containers. The ship made its inaugural call at the Port of Kobe on 24 November, where a welcoming ceremony was held. Representatives from the Kobe City Port and Harbor Bureau and Hanshin Port presented commemorative gifts to Captain Tadahiro Yabuta. Minato measures 96.81 metres in length and 14 metres in width. It has a gross tonnage of 749 tonnes and a deadweight of 1,711 tonnes. The vessel is powered by a 2,600 PS Hanshin Diesel Works LA34G main engine. Imoto Lines said the new vessel will support the expansion of maritime container transport through the modal shift of international feeder and domestic cargo. The carrier aims to contribute to lower energy consumption, reduced logistics costs and greater route diversification within Japan’s distribution network.

articles.title: APM Terminals and Port of Rotterdam prepare terminal expansion
articles.summary: APM Terminals Maasvlakte II and the Port of Rotterdam Authority are preparing a new phase of expansion at the Maasvlakte II container terminal. articles.body: APM Terminals Maasvlakte II and the Port of Rotterdam Authority are preparing a new phase of expansion at the Maasvlakte II container terminal. It will add 25 hectares of terminal area, about 711 metres of additional quay and supporting port infrastructure, and is expected to raise annual capacity by roughly 1.4 million TEU once complete. The terminal has been investing in its facilities at Prinses Amaliahaven since 2008, and the expansion is being delivered in phases while the existing terminal stays fully operational. The first part has recently come into service. The two organisations will divide the work. APM Terminals Maasvlakte II will concentrate on developing terminal operations, while the Port of Rotterdam Authority, in cooperation with the terminal, will prepare the site for construction and deliver the maritime infrastructure. That includes extending the existing quay wall by 711 metres and the landside crane rail by 428 metres, and dredging about 1.3 million cubic metres of sand. The new infrastructure will add capacity for deepsea, feeder and inland shipping vessels. The terminal is fully automated, with electrified equipment, automated guided vehicles and remotely operated quay cranes. Harold Kunst, Managing Director of APM Terminals Maasvlakte II, called the expansion the next step in the terminal’s long-term development, creating space for future growth while continuing to serve customers safely, reliably and efficiently, and said the collaboration with the Port Authority is essential. Boudewijn Siemons, CEO of the Port of Rotterdam Authority, said the investment in additional capacity and modern infrastructure strengthens Rotterdam’s position as Europe’s leading container port, increases the resilience of logistics chains, contributes to security of supply and supports the competitiveness of the Dutch economy.

articles.title: Construction of a new logistics area awarded at Vibo Valentia Marina
articles.summary: Paolo Piacenza, President of the Southern Tyrrhenian and Ionian Sea Port Authority, has signed the decree awarding the demolition of the former Civam industrial building and the construction of a new commercial logistics area beside the Bengasi dock in the port of Vibo Valentia Marina. articles.body: Paolo Piacenza, President of the Southern Tyrrhenian and Ionian Sea Port Authority, has signed the decree awarding the demolition of the former Civam industrial building and the construction of a new commercial logistics area beside the Bengasi dock in the port of Vibo Valentia Marina. The project has a total value of EUR 1.5 million. Following a competitive tender, the contract went to La Martina Appalti Srls of Villa Literno, in the province of Caserta, for EUR 863,887. Work is due to start within days and will last 180 days from delivery of the site. The works involve complete demolition of the old industrial warehouse and the subsequent construction of new yards to support port handling and logistics activities. This reclaims a space now occupied by a defunct structure and returns it to a use consistent with the port’s operational needs. Its strategic position near the Bengasi dock will improve the organisation of port spaces, make commercial activities more efficient and strengthen the port’s ability to meet the needs of operators and the local production system. The project belongs to the 2026-2028 Three-Year Operational Plan and to a wider development strategy for the port, which includes investments to upgrade infrastructure, improve the efficiency of port spaces, raise security and strengthen links between the port, economic activities and the surrounding area. The transformation aims to make Vibo Valentia Marina more functional, competitive and integrated with the local manufacturing sector by reclaiming existing areas and creating spaces suited to the new needs of commercial ports. Piacenza described the redevelopment as a concrete step in the modernisation and revitalisation of the port, saying the area can be fully restored to its former port function and used for strategic commercial logistics services. He said the goal is to make the port more efficient and better equipped, supporting local economic activity and creating new development opportunities.

articles.summary: Diana Shipping Inc., a global shipping company specializing in the ownership and bareboat charter-in of dry bulk vessels, today announced key changes to its leadership structure, including the appointment of Christos Tsakonas as Chief Investments and Strategy Officer effective November 23, 2026. articles.body: Diana Shipping Inc. Announces Key Leadership Appointment and Organizational Changes to Support its Long-Term Strategy in Hellenic Shipping News 25/11/2026 Diana Shipping Inc., a global shipping company specializing in the ownership and bareboat charter-in of dry bulk vessels, today announced key changes to its leadership structure, including the appointment of Christos Tsakonas as Chief Investments and Strategy Officer effective November 23, 2026. In this role, Mr. Tsakonas will be responsible for overseeing the Company’s investment strategy and financing activities, reporting directly to Semiramis Paliou, Director and Chief Executive Officer of Diana Shipping Inc. Mr. Tsakonas began his career at JPMorgan in London before spending 18 years with DNB in different locations and most recently in Oslo, Norway, where he served as Global Head of Shipping. During his tenure, he played a significant role in strengthening and expanding DNB’s position as one of the leading financial institutions in the global shipping industry. He brings to Diana extensive experience in shipping finance, investment banking and strategic leadership, together with an in-depth understanding of the global shipping industry and its financial markets. He will be based in Athens, Greece. As part of the Company’s evolution of the leadership structure, effective March 1, 2027, Ioannis Zafirakis will step down from his position as President of the Company and transition to an advisory role. He will remain a member of the Company’s Board of Directors and of the Executive Committee, continuing to provide strategic guidance and the benefit of his extensive experience, his institutional knowledge, as well as his expertise in capital markets and the shipping industry. In his advisory role, Mr. Zafirakis will work closely with Mr. Lefteris Papatrifon, who has served on the Board of Directors and Executive Committee since 2023. Commenting on the changes, Semiramis Paliou, Director and Chief Executive Officer of Diana Shipping Inc., said: “Our strategy and priorities remain unchanged. These organizational changes reflect an evolution of our leadership structure, bringing together complementary experience and expertise to support Diana’s continued development and long-term objectives. Christos brings significant international shipping finance and strategic experience, while Ioannis’s ongoing involvement ensures Diana continues to benefit from his strong knowledge of the Company. Together with Christos, Ioannis and Lefteris, we look forward to building on Diana’s strong foundation and pursuing our long-term objectives.” Mr. Tsakonas: “I am delighted to join Diana Shipping at such an important time in the Company’s development. Diana has established a strong reputation and a distinguished position in the global shipping industry, and I look forward to supporting Semiramis and contributing to the Company’s next phase of development,” said Mr. Tsakonas. Mr. Zafirakis: “I am pleased to welcome Christos to our team. Together we will continue to build on the company’s success delivering on our long term strategy.,” said Mr. Zafirakis. Mr. Papatrifon: “I look forward to continuing to work in close partnership with Ioannis, supporting Diana’s CEO, Semiramis, in advancing the Company’s strategic objectives,” said Mr. Papatrifon. articles.body: SUARDIAZ Group welcomes RS Atlantico to Zeebrugge as new vessel joins Atlantic Line in International Shipping News 25/11/2026 SUARDIAZ Group has welcomed its new vessel, RS Atlantico, to Zeebrugge as the 5,500-CEU PCTC begins operations on the company’s Atlantic Line. Customers, partners, industry representatives and SUARDIAZ Group executives, led by CEO Juan Riva, gathered in Zeebrugge to mark the vessel’s arrival in Europe and see its capabilities first-hand. RS Atlantico joins three vessels currently operating on the Atlantic Line, which connects Morocco, Spain, the UK, France and Belgium and serves major automotive manufacturers. Its addition increases SUARDIAZ Shipping Lines’ capacity to transport vehicles and other rolling cargo. SUARDIAZ Group has invested significantly in its inbound logistics operations, including a fleet of more than 500 trucks and a new terminal in Liverpool, UK. The addition of RS Atlantico strengthens the outbound side of its automotive logistics operations. The new vessel builds on SUARDIAZ Group’s ongoing investment in its shipping fleet, adding greater capacity to support customers, pursue new business opportunities and strengthen its maritime services. “The addition of RS Atlantico to our Atlantic Line turns our ongoing investment strategy into operational capacity. For SUARDIAZ Group, growth is not simply about adding new assets, but about having greater capacity and better tools to support our customers in an increasingly global and demanding industry,” said Juan Riva, CEO of SUARDIAZ Group. RS Atlantico is a 190-metre PCTC (Pure Car and Truck Carrier) with an approximate capacity of 5,500 CEU and 55,000 GT. It is designed to transport vehicles, machinery and High & Heavy cargo, expanding the operational capabilities of SUARDIAZ Shipping Lines. The vessel is also equipped with a dual-fuel propulsion system capable of operating on liquefied natural gas (LNG), a transitional technology within the ongoing technological and environmental evolution of maritime transport. The arrival of RS Atlantico in Zeebrugge reflects the port’s importance to SUARDIAZ’s Atlantic Line and the wider European automotive industry. Part of the Port of Antwerp-Bruges, Zeebrugge is a major hub for European RoRo and automotive traffic, with strong maritime connectivity, proximity to major European markets and links with the UK. articles.body: Transpetro carries out Suape’s first B30 bunkering in International Shipping News 25/11/2026 Petrobras’ shipping and logistics subsidiary Transpetro carried out the first B30 bunkering operation at Brazil’s Port of Suape on 22 November. Transpetro supplied 520 mt of B30 to the crude oil tanker Castro Alves, which is part of its own fleet. The blend comprised 30% biofuel and 70% VLSFO, and was delivered by barge at the port’s Liquid Bulk Pier 3B. A second biofuel bunkering operation is expected this week. The operation makes Suape the second Brazilian port to join Petrobras’ Green Route project, which aims to expand the company’s bio-bunkering operations in Brazil. Suape has also become the only port in the country’s North and Northeast regions to supply biofuel bunker blends, according to Armando Monteiro Bisneto, director-president of the Suape Port and Industrial Complex. Petrobras plans to introduce biofuel bunkering at the ports of Rio Grande, Santos and São Sebastião through 2026 and 2027. Ahead of the first delivery, the tanker Queen of Doria delivered blending components to Suape on 11 November, sufficient to produce up to 8,000 mt of B30. The cargo included B100 biodiesel sourced from Aratu, Bahia, and VLSFO, according to the port authority. “The project aims to expand the infrastructure for supplying Petrobras fleets with fuel blends containing renewable components and thereby reduce the carbon intensity of maritime transport,” the port authority said. articles.body: Houthis threaten Saudi ports amid Yemen conflict escalation in Port News 25/11/2026 Yemen’s Houthi movement warned Wednesday that the Saudi port of Jeddah and all other Saudi ports along the Red Sea coast would be targeted if Saudi Arabia moved to attack the Yemeni port of Hodeidah. Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree issued a statement urging port employees, workers, and nearby residents to evacuate immediately. The group also called on shipping companies to remove their vessels from the area. Following the Houthi warning, the Saudi-led coalition said it struck operational capabilities at Hodeidah and destroyed several targets in the Yemeni governorates of Saada and Amran. The exchange follows a Houthi drone strike Tuesday on the tallest tower in Riyadh, which Saudi authorities said injured at least 11 people. The Saudi-led coalition vowed a firm response to that attack. Hodeidah is the main entry point for food and essential supplies into Houthi-controlled northern Yemen. The port has long served as a critical channel for humanitarian aid and commercial imports for millions of Yemenis in a country heavily dependent on imported goods. Clashes between the two sides have intensified since September, when the Houthis advanced toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a key shipping passage at the southern entrance to the Red Sea. Since then, the Houthis have increased strikes on Saudi airports, ports, and oil facilities, while Saudi Arabia has stepped up airstrikes on Houthi positions inside Yemen. articles.body: PSA Vietnam And Lach Huyen International Logistics & Industrial Park Break Ground For New Container Terminal In Hai Phong in Port News 25/11/2026 PSA Vietnam (PSA) and Lach Huyen International Logistics & Industrial Park (LHF) marked the groundbreaking of their new container terminal at Lach Huyen, Hai Phong, North Vietnam on 23 November 2026. With an annual handling capacity of 4.7 million twenty-foot equivalent units (TEUs), the terminal will strengthen North Vietnam’s port infrastructure and connectivity to global markets. Operating as Haiphong Xuan Cau PSA International Container Terminal (HXPICT), the terminal combines PSA’s port management expertise and global network with LHF’s industrial park and hinterland assets. Together, this forms an integrated ecosystem that connects North Vietnam’s hinterland with the terminal and PSA’s global network. Nelson Quek, Regional CEO, Southeast Asia, PSA International, said, “The development of HXPICT is an important milestone in advancing PSA’s Node to Network strategy, which seeks to connect ports and supply chain hubs into an integrated global network. This collaboration strengthens PSA’s presence in North Vietnam and expands our network across key markets and trade routes, enabling us to better connect regional markets with global trade flows. We look forward to working with LHF to realise the terminal’s potential and support the continued growth of Vietnam’s trade and maritime sector.” Mr Nguyen Vinh Hau, General Director of LHF, said, “Today’s groundbreaking marks the beginning of a port infrastructure project of strategic significance to Hai Phong and the wider northern economic region. Together with our partner PSA, we are committed to delivering the project on schedule, ensuring quality and safety, bringing the first two berths into operation in 2028, and integrating the deepwater port with the non-tariff zone and industrial park into a coordinated logistics ecosystem that will enhance the competitiveness of Vietnamese goods.” Source: PSA Vietnam 2026-11-25 hellenicshippingnews... tweet Share

articles.body: Imported iron ore margins increased on firmer port spot prices – Shanghai Metals Market (SMM) in Commodity News 25/11/2026 The average imported iron ore margin rose from -8.78 yuan/mt to -4.30 yuan/mt. The increase was mainly driven by higher port spot prices. On the supply side, domestic ore concentrators in the Tangshan area have made no clear progress in resuming production. Iron ore concentrate supply remained tight, and local prices were largely stable. On the demand side, SMM data showed hot metal output lost to blast furnace maintenance was 1.8182 million mt in the week ended November 20, down 6,400 mt week-on-week, with maintenance largely unchanged. Most mills in Tangshan were operating normally, and environmental curbs had a limited impact on blast furnaces. Rigid demand for iron ore remained supported. Futures edged higher for several sessions, but mill inquiries were few and spot trading was thin. High port inventories continued to cap upside. articles.summary: The US announced plans to impose a fresh round of tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and a dozen other economies under President Donald Trump’s push to restore sweeping global import taxes that the Supreme Court found unconstitutional.

BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/Pool via REUTERS/File Photo By Alicia Diaz (Bloomberg) –The US announced plans to impose a fresh round of tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and a dozen other economies under President Donald Trump’s push to restore sweeping global import taxes that the Supreme Court found unconstitutional. The rate for imports from China would rise to 20%, in line with the country’s prior agreement with the Trump administration — though that rate could double to 40% if talks between the two countries fall apart, according to a senior US official. The official briefed reporters on condition of anonymity ahead of Wednesday’s announcement. Products from the EU will be taxed at 15% in compliance with the US’s deal with the bloc, though that could also rise to as much as 20%, according to the Office of the US Trade Representative. Tariffs will apply to items from economies the Trump administration accuses of overproduction in some domestic industries and hurting American companies. They are still subject to a public comment process and could change. A final action could come as early as January, the official said. The new levies mark the latest effort by the administration to reinstate an expansive tariff agenda that included country-by-country levies implemented using emergency powers. Those were struck down by high-court justices in February, forcing Trump to invoke other legal authorities to advance his agenda. It’s a politically risky move. Democrats swept to a landslide victory in the midterm elections earlier this month thanks in part to voter anger over the cost of living and disapproval of the president’s handling of the economy. China and the EU could also retaliate, though initial signals from them were muted. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a briefing earlier Wednesday that the prospect of new US tariffs on its exports was “political maneuvering” and said the two nations should work together to maintain their trade truce. The announcement appears to comply with the 2025 trade agreement between the US and EU, which capped tariffs at 15% on most of the bloc’s exports. As a result, the move likely won’t antagonize transatlantic relations for now. European Commission spokesman Olof Gill said “we strongly reject the premise that Europe is a source of structural overcapacity” and added the bloc expects new levies to abide by the tariff agreement. US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said the new duties were designed to preserve existing deals while addressing overcapacity concerns. “A lot of these deals we made actually solve a lot of the problems we see in excess capacity or can go toward it,” Greer said Wednesday on CNBC. “We’ve talked to our trading partners about this. They know what we’re proposing. I think a lot of this is baked in.” Imports from Japan, South Korea, Switzerland — all prominent US trading partners — would be hit with a 15% rate. The number could go up to 25% for Korea and 20% for the other two, USTR said. Indian products would face a 17% charge if a trade pact with Washington is finalized, though that could increase to 25%. Several smaller nations in Asia were also hit. Similar expected measures aimed at Mexico and Norway were not included but remain under consideration, the official said. Greer said on CNBC the US has “had some very good conversations with Mexico” on the issue. The tariffs follow a probe that began in March into alleged excess manufacturing capacity, utilizing Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, a process seen as more resistant to legal challenges than Trump’s prior tariff wall. The tariff rates aren’t expected to surpass already agreed-upon levels in trade agreements with each economy. The move will test the tolerance of economic partners, who have largely held back from retaliating, opting instead to negotiate deals with the US to minimize their tariffs. That dynamic could be on display next month, when Trump meets again with his Chinese counterpart, Xi Jinping, on the sidelines of the Group of 20 summit. Their trade truce is set to expire in January unless the two powers agree to extend it. “If we were to go beyond the 20% or something like that, they would view that as breaking our deal,” Greer said, The trade ambassador said Washington and Beijing are also “proposing to implement” tariff reductions under its new board of trade on around $30 billion of non-sensitive exports. Greer signaled that the new levy will not stack on top of existing duties of 10% or 12.5% under a separate investigation into negligent enforcement of forced-labor laws. “Those are not really additive,” he said on CNBC. For products eligible to be hit by both sets of duties, only the higher rate would apply, the official said earlier. The official added that there would be goods exempted from the tariffs, including oil and gas and food products that cannot be grown in the US. Other products that are already subject to sectoral duties, including tariffs on pharmaceuticals and critical minerals, are also exempted. After the Supreme Court loss, Trump immediately announced plans to rebuild his tariff wall under a different legal authority. Under the Section 301 framework, the president can implement tariffs following an investigation into allegedly unfair foreign trading practices. While Section 301 tariffs are seen as more legally sound and flexible than other powers Trump has eyed, they’re also more time-consuming. An earlier investigation under the same legal authority into policies around forced labor from US trading partners resulted in tariffs on some 60 economies. Those duties are currently facing legal challenges. The new tariffs apply to Bangladesh, Cambodia, China, the European Union, India, Indonesia, Japan, Korea, Malaysia, Singapore, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, and Vietnam. USTR also announced it is raising tariffs on imports from Brazil, altering a previously-conducted trade investigation into the country’s digital policies and trade practices. The US is considering increasing the out-of-quota tariff rate on raw and refined sugar and proposing a 10% tariff on finished aircraft. The increased levy on imports from Brazil comes weeks after Trump ally Flavio Bolsonaro lost his presidential election bid to progressive incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. © 2026 Bloomberg L.P. Join the leading maritime news network Photo courtesy IMO The International Maritime Organization (IMO) is calling on shipping companies to make more training berths available to cadets, highlighting a longstanding disconnect between the industry’s need for qualified seafarers and the lack of opportunities for young people to gain the sea time required to enter the profession. In many developing countries, aspiring officers complete their shore-based maritime education only to spend years waiting for an onboard training placement, even as shipping companies struggle to recruit qualified personnel. In an announcement Tuesday, the IMO outlined efforts to expand its NextWave Seafarers initiative, which aims to address the bottleneck through cooperation between governments, shipowners and maritime training institutions. More than 80 participants representing over 25 countries gathered at IMO headquarters in London on November 20 to formally launch the second phase of the initiative and explore ways to increase the availability of onboard training opportunities. The program’s pilot phase, developed in partnership with Saudi Arabia’s Transport General Authority and national shipping company Bahri, saw 19 cadets from developing island nations and least developed countries complete their onboard training aboard Bahri vessels. The second phase aims to train at least 30 additional cadets, with women accounting for half of participants. The IMO also wants to recruit at least five shipping companies to provide training berths, laying the groundwork for a wider international partnership. The workshop examined practical barriers to cadet placements, including visa restrictions complicating crew changes, as well as the importance of providing a safe and supportive working environment for young seafarers entering the industry. The shortage of training berths exposes a fundamental challenge in addressing the industry’s workforce needs. Expanding maritime education alone will do little to increase the supply of qualified officers if graduates cannot secure the mandatory sea time needed to earn their professional credentials. Without sufficient participation from shipowners, the industry risks leaving a pool of prospective seafarers untapped at a time when it needs to attract and retain the next generation of maritime professionals. Photo courtesy EUNAVFOR Countries bordering the Red Sea and Western Indian Ocean are moving toward establishing a combined maritime task force to combat piracy, strengthen regional security and protect commercial shipping across some of the world’s most strategically important waterways. The International Maritime Organization (IMO) announced that signatories to the Djibouti Code of Conduct and its Jeddah Amendment have adopted a new Regional Maritime Security Strategy and agreed to advance plans for a Combined Maritime Task Force (CMTF). The agreement was reached during a high-level meeting held November 11–13 in Antananarivo, Madagascar. The proposed task force would build on existing national and regional maritime security capabilities, improving coordination among participating countries. Governments agreed to develop the force’s legal framework and concept of operations in 2027. The initiative comes amid persistent threats to commercial shipping in the Red Sea and renewed concerns over piracy off the Horn of Africa, underscoring the need for greater regional cooperation in protecting international trade and seafarers. The broader security strategy covers the Western Indian Ocean, Gulf of Aden and Red Sea. Preparatory work began in Saudi Arabia in November 2024, with government representatives, navies, coast guards and maritime law enforcement agencies subsequently meeting in Mombasa, Kenya, earlier this month to finalize the framework. Originally adopted in 2009 in response to Somali piracy, the Djibouti Code of Conduct was expanded in 2017 through the Jeddah Amendment to address a wider range of maritime security threats. Somalia’s Minister of State Mohamed Abdulkadir Mohamed emphasized the human cost of attacks on commercial shipping during the meeting. “The protection of seafarers is not simply a maritime security obligation; it is a fundamental humanitarian responsibility,” he said. The meeting also marked a leadership milestone, with Tanzania’s Stella Katondo becoming the first woman elected to chair the regional initiative. South Africa will serve as deputy chair. While the agreement represents a significant step toward a more coordinated regional security presence, the proposed task force remains in development. The IMO has not announced a deployment timeline or details of participating naval assets. articles.title: PIL and Qingdao Port complete China’s first bio-LNG bunkering for international shipping
articles.summary: Pacific International Lines (PIL) and Qingdao Port have completed what they describe as China’s first liquefied bio-methane (LBM) bunkering operation for an internationally trading vessel. The operation took place at Qingdao Port’s QQCTN terminal, where PIL’s LNG dual-fuel containership Kota Odyssey received...
articles.body: Pacific International Lines (PIL) and Qingdao Port have completed what they describe as China’s first liquefied bio-methane (LBM) bunkering operation for an internationally trading vessel. The operation took place at Qingdao Port’s QQCTN terminal, where PIL’s LNG dual-fuel containership Kota Odyssey received ISCC-certified LBM through a truck-to-ship transfer. It also marks the Singapore-based carrier’s first use of the renewable fuel in its fleet. Produced from organic feedstocks, LBM, also known as bio-LNG, can be used in LNG dual-fuel engines without modifying the vessels’ existing machinery. PIL is introducing the fuel as part of its efforts to reduce shipping emissions while expanding its fleet of dual-fuel containerships. According to the carrier, the batch supplied at Qingdao is expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by more than 70% compared with conventional fuel oil, based on a well-to-wake lifecycle assessment. PIL also estimates a reduction of around 70% compared with fossil LNG. PIL advances alternative fuel adoption The bunkering operation represents a further step in PIL’s fleet decarbonisation programme, which combines new vessel investments with energy-efficiency technologies and the gradual introduction of lower-emission fuels. Since 2022, the company has ordered 28 LNG dual-fuel containerships, providing greater flexibility to adopt renewable alternatives as commercial supplies increase. “This milestone demonstrates the flexibility PIL has built into our fleet renewal programme,” said Abhishek Chawla, Chief Marine Officer, PIL. The vessel involved, Kota Odyssey, was delivered to PIL in 2024 and operates on the carrier’s SWS service connecting Asia and West Africa. For Qingdao Port, the operation demonstrates its ability to supply renewable LNG alternatives to international shipping companies. The port is working to expand its alternative fuel services as demand for lower-emission marine fuels develops. “This maiden biomethane bunkering service is a major milestone for China’s green shipping transition,” said Yijie Zhang, Head of the Energy Business Department, Ark Intelligence, Qingdao Port. Zhang added that the partnership with PIL supports Qingdao’s development as a regional green bunkering hub. The companies did not disclose the volume of LBM supplied during the operation or the commercial terms of the bunkering arrangement.

Finnish Border Guard/Handout via REUTERS ROME, Nov 25 (Reuters) – Italy has told Ukraine it was wrong to attack Russian ships in Libyan waters and warned Kyiv not to spread the war to new areas, Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani told Corriere della Sera newspaper on Wednesday. “It was a mistake to violate Libya’s sovereignty,” Tajani said, adding that Rome had received no advance warning of the Ukrainian operations. “Italy was absolutely unaware of Kyiv’s intentions to strike in Libyan territorial waters, even inside a port,” said the minister, who is head of the coalition Forza Italia party. Another coalition party, the far-right League, also condemned the attack, calling it “unacceptable” and warning that it risked destabilising the north African country. Italy has been a staunch supporter of Ukraine since Russia’s 2022 invasion, providing military aid and backing European sanctions against Moscow. However, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s government has sent mixed signals, with her own party firmly behind Kyiv while the League, led by Matteo Salvini, has repeatedly criticised continued military assistance to Ukraine. Tajani said that Rome would carry on supporting Kyiv’s sovereignty while seeking to prevent the conflict from spreading. “Italy will remain on Ukraine’s side. Ours is a strategic choice,” he said. articles.summary: A record 2,100-plus migrants arrived in Spain's Canary Islands over 24 hours in overcrowded boats, maritime rescue service data showed on Wednesday, prompting regional leader Fernando Clavijo to call for a European-level response to the crisis."The Canaries can't take it anymore.
articles.body: Canary Islands Receive Recording-Breaking Number of Migrants In Single Day Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 © Adobe Stock/Halina A record 2,100-plus migrants arrived in Spain's Canary Islands over 24 hours in overcrowded boats, maritime rescue service data showed on Wednesday, prompting regional leader Fernando Clavijo to call for a European-level response to the crisis. "The Canaries can't take it anymore. We're experiencing an unprecedented migration pressure," Clavijo wrote on X, adding that he had requested an urgent meeting with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. "These people come to Europe and it's not fair that we alone respond to a drama of this magnitude," he said. One migrant was found dead in a boat and another gave birth during the perilous crossing from West Africa, the rescue service said. The daily arrivals surpassed the previous record of about 1,500 set two weeks ago. Most of the boats arrived at El Hierro, an island of some 11,400 residents that has become one of Europe's key entry points for migrants from West Africa. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez, who has faced tough criticism of his open stance on migration during the campaign ahead of Sunday's parliamentary election, said on Wednesday Europe needed a comprehensive approach to migration, including stronger border controls in cooperation with Senegalese and Gambian authorities. Still, he said Spain needed "to open legal migration pathways" for workers in sectors such as housing that are short of qualified labour. The Atlantic route from West Africa to the Canary Islands is one of the world's deadliest migration crossings as migrants seek to reach Spanish territory despite rough seas, strong currents and long distances. Arrivals tend to pick up in the autumn months, when sea conditions along the route are generally calmer and more favourable for crossings. Arrivals so far this year had climbed to 28,103 as of late November, more than last year's total but still well below an all-time high of 46,843 recorded in 2024, when most crossings occurred during the first nine months of the year. Nearly 21,000 people have reached the archipelago in the last two months. (Reuters)

articles.title: Houston Ship Channel trade grows
articles.summary: Trade activity across the Houston Ship Channel region continued to grow, reinforcing the waterway’s role in supporting American industry, jobs and economic activity. Foreign tonnage rose 15% year to date through September to 200.2 million tons, driven by a 20% rise in exports, and deep draft vessel transits increased...
articles.body: Trade activity across the Houston Ship Channel region continued to grow, reinforcing the waterway’s role in supporting American industry, jobs and economic activity. Foreign tonnage rose 15% year to date through September to 200.2 million tons, driven by a 20% rise in exports, and deep draft vessel transits increased 12% in October. The region remains central to US energy exports. Through September, Houston accounted for 32% of US crude oil exports and nearly 65% of the year-to-date increase in national oil exports, with the Netherlands, Mexico and Japan its three leading destinations. Domestic cargo is also significant: based on US Army Corps of Engineers indicators and historical data, Port Houston estimates that 67.6 million short tons moved through the region in the first nine months of 2026, up about 3.8% from an estimated 65.1 million short tons a year earlier. At Port Houston’s public terminals, October container volume reached 415,326 TEUs, up 14 percent year on year and the highest October on record. Loaded imports hit an all-time monthly high of 199,302 TEUs, surpassing the previous record set in May, and loaded exports climbed to an October record of 144,334 TEUs. Through the first ten months of 2026 the port handled a record 3.76 million TEUs, up 4%. Growth extended beyond containers: steel tonnage at the public terminals increased 74% to 504,010 tons, and general cargo rose 170% to 217,633 tons, with steel, packaged cement and other industrial materials supporting construction, manufacturing and energy-related industries. Charlie Jenkins, CEO of Port Houston, described the Houston Ship Channel as an economic engine for the region, supporting jobs and businesses across Texas and the nation, with the industries along it moving the goods and materials that keep the economy running.

articles.title: NYK Line, Partners to Advance Remote Ship Emissions Monitoring
articles.summary: Shipping company NYK Line and seven other organizations have signed an agreement to develop remote sensing technology capable of measuring greenhouse gas emissions from vessels without physical contact, with trials focused on Yokohama Port in Japan.The agreement…
articles.body: NYK Line, Partners to Advance Remote Ship Emissions Monitoring Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 Conceptual image of the system (Credit: NYK Line) Shipping company NYK Line and seven other organizations have signed an agreement to develop remote sensing technology capable of measuring greenhouse gas emissions from vessels without physical contact, with trials focused on Yokohama Port in Japan. The agreement, signed on November 25, brings together NYK Line, MUFG Bank, Nagoya Electric Works, ArkEdge Space, Shimizu Corporation, the City of Yokohama, Yokohama-Kawasaki International Port Corporation and Yokohama Port Corporation. The collaboration will advance the True Emission Eye - Maritime project, which aims to develop technology for measuring, visualizing and quantifying greenhouse gas emissions from ships at a distance. The project will conduct measurements on actual vessels at Yokohama Port to assess the technology's accuracy, while examining system specifications, potential applications and opportunities for future commercial deployment. The technology is being developed to complement existing methods of estimating vessel emissions based on fuel type and consumption, providing a means of directly measuring emissions from outside ships. The system uses optical observation technology that exploits the ability of gases, including carbon dioxide, to absorb and emit light at specific wavelengths. Data obtained from vessel exhaust observations is combined with physical parameters, including distance to the ship and weather conditions, to calculate emissions. Testing has already been conducted at experimental facilities and on NYK Group vessels, both at berth and underway. At Yokohama Port, the project has captured infrared images of ship exhaust from observation points including Osanbashi Pier and the Yokohama Bay Bridge Skywalk. The images are being compared and analyzed against vessel data to evaluate the technology. The partners will continue conducting measurements under different conditions to improve the accuracy of the system, while also examining fixed-point monitoring at ports. The project will also assess the technical requirements for satellite-based observations of ship emissions and explore the potential integration of satellite measurements with ground-based data. The eight organizations aim to bring the technology into practical use to improve transparency in vessel emissions reporting and support decarbonization across the shipping and port sectors.

articles.body: The Port of Oakland and WattEV, a leading provider of heavy-duty charging infrastructure, have opened a new heavy-duty electric truck charging depot at the port, the first of its kind in Northern California. Officials also announced the purchase of 300 electric Tesla Semi trucks to serve the port, with the first batch due before the end of the year and the balance in 2027. According to WattEV, at current high diesel prices the operating costs of these electric trucks are half those of comparable diesels. The trucks will help establish a zero-emission freight corridor from the Bay Area to Sacramento, the Central Valley, Nevada and beyond, and the depot forms part of the port’s continued electrification. The depot, at 8407 Edgewater Drive, can charge 25 medium- and heavy-duty electric trucks at once at up to 240 kW each, or seven trucks at 1.2 MW. It is designed for megawatt charging, which cuts dwell times to 30 minutes or less, comparable to diesel refuelling. The opening ceremony was attended by partners including WattEV, the Bay Area Air District, the California Energy Commission and PG&E, together with guests from the California Air Resources Board and other agencies. Port of Oakland Executive Director Kristi McKenney said real progress is under way in changing how goods move to and from the seaport, with industry partners delivering projects that support cleaner freight, healthier communities and a more sustainable future. Mayor Barbara Lee called the opening a significant milestone, shaped directly by community input, that shows Oakland’s role as a centre of green innovation and ensures neighbourhoods disproportionately affected by pollution benefit from the investment. WattEV CEO and co-founder Salim Youssefzadeh noted that most truck charging infrastructure has so far been concentrated in Southern California, and said the partnership gives Northern California truckers an electric transport ecosystem that can outperform traditional diesel hauling.

The four vessels will be equipped with Wärtsilä 25 engines, following the selection of the same engine type for the first two EasyMax 2.0 ships in 2025, the Finnish technology group announced on November 25. Each engine will also be equipped with Wärtsilä's NOx Reducer (NOR) emissions after-treatment system, which uses selective catalytic reduction technology to reduce nitrogen oxide emissions. The engine selection forms part of Wagenborg's EasyMax 2.0 design, which focuses on fuel efficiency, operational flexibility and reduced emissions. Wagenborg operates a fleet of more than 160 vessels, with Wärtsilä equipment installed on over half of them. The companies also maintain a long-term service agreement covering engines and propulsion systems across Wagenborg's fleet. articles.summary: A record three-quarters of the global fleet of large tankers designed to transport oil products are tapping higher earnings to ship crude, keeping the cost to move fuels elevated.

Join the leading maritime news network Photo: Avigator Thailand/Shutterstock By Weilun Soon Nov 25, 2026 (Bloomberg) –A record three-quarters of the global fleet of large tankers designed to transport oil products are tapping higher earnings to ship crude, keeping the cost to move fuels elevated. Less than a quarter of the world’s 542 long-range 2, or LR2, tankers are currently transporting “clean” cargoes such as jet fuel, naphtha and diesel as of this week, according to Signal Ocean data. The vessels have cargo holds that are coated to transport refined fuels, and have to undergo an expensive cleaning process to return to the trade once they ship “dirty” crude oil. The shift in use of the LR2 fleet comes as crude flows recover through the Strait of Hormuz. A system of shuttling tankers and ship-to-ship transfers has helped exports from the Persian Gulf recover to pre-war levels, boosting freight rates and prompting charterers to tap smaller vessels to meet demand. Benchmark earnings for very-large crude carriers have soared, in turn enabling smaller-sized tankers — including Aframaxes, which are the crude-focused equivalent of LR2s, able to hold about 750,000 barrels — to command far higher fees. And an LR2 that dirties up can charge Aframax earnings. Shipping executives often look at how many LR2s are switching to plan on how much they can charge, and how they should deploy their tankers around the world. Even though the LR2 fleet has grown 12% since January last year and clean-fuel shipments have fallen due to the US-Iran war, the increased switching to crude has helped put a floor underneath the fees they can command to carry oil products. “Tracking LR2 employment between clean and dirty trades is becoming as important as monitoring the size of the fleet itself,” Signal analysts Maria Bertzeletou and Georgios Sakellariou said. The switching of LR2s started last year as traders sought to store more crude on vessels at sea, but accelerated in the initial phase of the Iran War from the end of February, when refineries in the Middle East were attacked by the Islamic Republic — reducing the need for clean tankers, Sakellariou said. Read More: Oil Tankers Get ‘Dirty’ Ditching Fuels for Crude as Rates Boom A lot of the processing plants in the region remain unavailable, reducing the need for products tankers. About 1.7 million out of the more than 9 million barrels a day of refining capacity is currently offline in the Middle East, RBC Capital Markets analysts including Christopher Louney and Helima Croft wrote in a note this week. Around 1 million barrels a day of that potentially needs months to repair, they said. Charterers are turning to smaller product tankers, with the share of LR2s in transporting fuels falling to just 12% between July and September, from almost 18% a year earlier, Signal data show. Meanwhile, a benchmark freight index reflecting daily LR2 earnings from the Mediterranean to Asia increased more than five-fold, while another from the Middle East to Europe jumped more than 10-fold in the year through end-September. © 2026 Bloomberg L.P. Join the leading maritime news network On 24 November 2026, Windcat signed a contract with Damen Shipyards Group for the second Multi-Purpose Accommodation Support Vessel (MP-ASV) in the Innovation Series. The contract follows the order for the first vessel , with an option for five more, signed in November last year. Sound basis The MP-ASV is an entirely new type of vessel designed to support operations in the offshore energy industry . Its design draws heavily on Damen’s experience in the design and construction of Commissioning Services Operations Vessels (CSOVs). This includes the Elevation Series CSOVs, developed together by Damen and Windcat. The first vessel in the Elevation Series, Windcat Rotterdam , was presented with the KNVTS Ship of the Year Award at this year’s Maritime Awards Gala. The MP-ASV takes the proven capabilities of the Elevation Series CSOVs and builds on them further. Extended capabilities The MP-ASVs build on these capabilities in a number of ways, including with their 102 x 20 metre hull and its 750m 2 deck space. The MP-ASV is able to assist and operate in all offshore energy markets, including cable repair, flotel functions, offshore wind and ROV assistance. Additionally, the vessel is fitted with 111 cabins, allowing up to 190 persons on board. The vessel features an offshore crane which can be used as a 150-tonne subsea crane, or as a 15-tonne 3D motion-compensated crane. The vessel can also be fitted with remotely operated vehicles (ROVs). The vessels are being equipped with a DP2+ system holding DNV CBS and CBT class notations, which cover a wider scope of redundant closed bus-ties system arrangements, for enhanced fault tolerance. The DP system features additional tunnel thrusters fore and aft to provide increased redundancy for safe operations in remote offshore locations. Access is via a 3D motion-compensated gangway with two exchangeable tips, one for short connections used in the wind industry and one capable of long continuous connections. Prepared for efficiency The MP-ASVs will be outfitted with a battery system to enable peak shaving, spinning reserve and electrical sailing. This will enable highly efficient operations, for example when in DP mode. Like the Windcat CSOVs, a key feature of the Innovation Series vessels is the integration of low-carbon fuels . Hence a dual fuel hydrogen auxiliary genset is installed, and the three main generator sets are of the next generation Evolve generator sets from ABC, which allow for a range of low-emission possibilities. These engines can operate on liquid fuels such as biodiesel and HVO, on dual fuel with pilot injection of liquid fuel, or on 100% gas using spark ignition. High offshore comfort level The design of the vessel is also highly focused on comfort for the up to 190 personnel onboard. Measures include well-thought-out routing, use of high-quality materials and aesthetically appealing accommodation. The aim is to make crew and personnel feel at home during extended periods of up to 150 days offshore, due to her extended fuel capacity. Strength-to-strength Damen Sales Director Joost van der Weiden says, “We are delighted to receive this second MP-ASV order from Windcat. The cooperation that began with our development of the Elevation Series continues to grow in strength. With the Innovation Series we mutually have developed a vessel that will further enhance Windcat’s capabilities to support its clients in the offshore energy industry in the years ahead.” Windcat Managing Director Willem van der Wel says: “The decision to order a second MP-ASV reflects our confidence in this new vessel concept and our ambition to further strengthen our position in the offshore energy market. By combining the capabilities of a multi-purpose support vessel with high-quality offshore accommodation, we are creating a versatile solution that responds to the evolving needs of our customers. Suksawat gives us a strong platform in Greater Bangkok, directly connected to some of the country’s and the region’s most important industrial and logistics corridors,” said Farid Belbouab, Group CEO of Gulftainer. Following the takeover, Gulftainer plans to strengthen the terminal’s capabilities and improve connections with Thailand’s industrial hinterland. The acquisition also creates opportunities to link the facility with the group’s wider port, logistics, industrial park and shipping activities. “Thailand is a new market for Gulftainer, but our ambition is long term. articles.title: Maersk, MSC and HMM raise the stakes in global fleet expansion
articles.summary: The latest wave of containership orders is putting future vessel supply back in the spotlight. Maersk, MSC and HMM account for nearly 80% of the capacity associated with orders recorded in Dynamar‘s November 2026 edition of DynaLiners Monthly. The report lists 83 containerships with a combined capacity of 938,500...
articles.body: The latest wave of containership orders is putting future vessel supply back in the spotlight. Maersk, MSC and HMM account for nearly 80% of the capacity associated with orders recorded in Dynamar ‘s November 2026 edition of DynaLiners Monthly. The report lists 83 containerships with a combined capacity of 938,500 TEU, excluding two additional vessel options. These orders were reported since the previous edition, with deliveries scheduled between 2028 and 2031. However, the distribution of this capacity reveals a particularly interesting trend. While investment continues across multiple vessel segments, three major carriers account for the overwhelming majority of the reported capacity. Three carriers account for nearly 80% of capacity Maersk represents the largest newbuilding programme listed in Dynamar’s November report. The publication records 24 containerships of 24,000 TEU at Hudong Zhonghua Shipbuilding, with deliveries scheduled for 2029 and 2030. Together, these vessels represent 576,000 TEU of nominal capacity, or approximately 61.4% of the total recorded in the report’s ordering section. Container News has previously covered Maersk’s reported plans for a major megamax newbuilding programme . Meanwhile, Dynamar lists eight 13,400 TEU containerships for HMM at HD Hyundai, scheduled for delivery in 2029. The programme represents a combined capacity of 107,200 TEU. The South Korean carrier’s broader fleet investment strategy has also been examined in previous Container News coverage . MSC appears in the report with three 21,000 TEU vessels at Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding. Deliveries are expected in 2028 and 2029. The reported investment reflects MSC’s continued interest in larger vessels, following its ongoing expansion of megamax newbuilding programmes . Based on Dynamar’s figures, the three carriers collectively account for 35 vessels and 746,200 TEU. Although these vessels represent approximately 42% of the ships listed, they account for 79.5% of the reported capacity. This concentration highlights how investment in larger containerships can significantly increase future vessel supply without a proportionate increase in fleet numbers. Regional carriers pursue a different strategy Despite the concentration of capacity among the largest carriers, investment in smaller vessels remains an important feature of the report. Regional Container Lines (RCL) is listed with six containerships across two size categories, representing a combined capacity of 30,800 TEU. Eastern Pacific is associated with four vessels of 6,000 and 9,000 TEU, totalling 30,000 TEU. Meanwhile, TS Lines features with two 11,000 TEU containerships. Regional operators are also securing smaller vessels to support their networks. Korea Marine Transport Company (KMTC), for example, is listed with six 3,100 TEU containerships at Huangpu Wenchong Shipbuilding. Container News previously covered the company’s first overseas newbuilding order . Similarly, Pacific International Lines (PIL) appears in the report with seven 1,400 TEU feeder containerships at Huanghai Shipbuilding. Independent shipowners, including Danaos, Peter Doehle and Global Ship Lease , also feature in the latest ordering activity. Overall, vessels below 4,000 TEU account for 34 of the 83 ships listed. However, they represent only 76,900 TEU, or approximately 8.2% of the reported capacity. The figures illustrate two distinct investment approaches. Larger containerships offer potential economies of scale, while smaller vessels provide greater operational flexibility. They can also support regional connectivity and services to ports with infrastructure limitations. Consequently, competition for future capacity extends beyond the largest vessels and the main East–West trade corridors. Reported containership orders and associated vessel capacity by selected companies. Source: Dynamar, DynaLiners Monthly, November 2026. Calculations and visualisation by Container News. Chinese shipyards dominate reported orders The geographical distribution of the newbuilding programmes highlights China’s position in the containership construction market. Chinese shipyards account for 69 of the 83 vessels listed by Dynamar. Their combined nominal capacity reaches 782,900 TEU, representing approximately 83.4% of the reported total. Hudong Zhonghua features prominently through the programmes attributed to Maersk and Danaos. Shanghai Waigaoqiao is associated with orders from MSC and TS Lines. Meanwhile, Huangpu Wenchong appears in programmes involving KMTC, RCL and Global Ship Lease. South Korea accounts for eight vessels through HMM’s programme at HD Hyundai. Japan accounts for four vessels through Eastern Pacific’s orders at Imabari Shipbuilding. The construction location remains undisclosed for two 9,200 TEU vessels attributed to RCL. These figures reflect the orders recorded in Dynamar’s November edition rather than the entire global containership orderbook. Nevertheless, they underline the strategic importance of Chinese shipbuilding capacity in the latest reported investment activity. For carriers and shipowners, securing construction slots several years in advance can provide greater control over fleet development. However, long delivery schedules also expose investors to changes in market conditions. New capacity enters a strong charter market While the latest orders target deliveries towards the end of the decade, new containership capacity continues to enter the market. According to Dynamar’s published totals, 21 containerships with a combined capacity of 169,200 TEU were delivered during October 2026. Approximately 94% of this capacity came from vessels exceeding 4,000 TEU. The largest deliveries included the 24,200 TEU OOCL Grace, the 16,600 TEU Ever Educe and the 16,100 TEU CMA CGM Lorenzaccio. At the same time, the containership charter market remained strong. The Harpex averaged 2,500 points in October, compared with 2,189 points in October 2025. Meanwhile, Braemar’s BOX Index increased from 268.4 to 322.8 over the same period. The latest readings included in Dynamar’s report placed both indices at their respective 2026 highs. Furthermore, all eight vessel categories tracked by the New ConTex recorded higher average charter rates in October compared with the same month a year earlier. The coexistence of new vessel deliveries and elevated charter rates suggests that incoming capacity has not eliminated demand for chartered tonnage. However, current charter market conditions do not necessarily indicate what the supply-demand balance will look like towards the end of the decade. The capacity challenge beyond 2028 The central question is whether future cargo demand will be sufficient to absorb the additional vessels. Larger containerships can reduce operating costs per container when utilisation remains high. However, weaker cargo demand could limit these economic advantages. Moreover, a widespread return to shorter shipping routes could release effective vessel capacity into the market. If this coincides with substantial newbuilding deliveries, carriers may face additional pressure to maintain vessel utilisation and freight rates. Several factors could influence the outcome, including fleet renewal, vessel recycling, sailing speeds and adjustments to service networks. Importantly, the capacity associated with reported orders should not be confused with net fleet growth. Some new vessels may replace older or less efficient tonnage rather than expand operating fleets. Nevertheless, Dynamar’s latest figures highlight the scale of future investment and its concentration among a small number of major carriers. For Maersk, MSC and HMM, the challenge will extend beyond securing larger fleets. These companies must ensure that future capacity matches the commercial requirements of their networks. Ultimately, the next phase of container shipping competition may depend less on which carrier controls the most capacity and more on which carrier deploys it most effectively.
takeaways: The latest wave of containership orders is putting future vessel supply back in the spotlight.
Maersk, MSC and HMM account for nearly 80% of the capacity associated with orders recorded in Dynamar ‘s November 2026 edition of DynaLiners Monthly.
The report lists 83 containerships with a combined capacity of 938,500 TEU, excluding two additional vessel options.

articles.title: Hong Kong shipowners hail shipping tax overhaul
articles.summary: The Hong Kong Shipowners Association (HKSOA) has welcomed a package of tax reforms aimed at attracting more shipping and commodity trading businesses to the city, including a new half-rate profits tax concession for physical commodity traders. articles.body: Greater China Operations Regulatory Hong Kong shipowners hail shipping tax overhaul Adis Ajdin November 25, 2026 0 202 1 minute read The Hong Kong Shipowners Association (HKSOA) has welcomed a package of tax reforms aimed at attracting more shipping and commodity trading businesses to the city, including a new half-rate profits tax concession for physical commodity traders. The measures, which returned to the Legislative Council for consideration on Wednesday, would reduce the profits tax rate on qualifying commodity trading activities from 16.5% to 8.25%, while expanding existing concessions for ship leasing, shipmanagement, ship agency and broking businesses. The legislation also introduces an optional 15% tax rate for qualifying shipping companies and commodity traders covered by the OECD’s global minimum tax rules, allowing them to simplify compliance under the BEPS 2.0 framework. For ship lessors, the changes include broader deductions for vessel acquisition costs and financing expenses, alongside greater flexibility in leasing arrangements. The commodity trading concession is designed to bring more trading houses to Hong Kong and generate additional demand for local shipping services. Under the proposed framework, eligible traders must meet minimum business turnover and local operating requirements, including conditions linking expenditure on maritime services to Hong Kong-based providers. The government has previously estimated that the concessions could generate HK$4.6bn ($590m) in economic benefits by encouraging commodity traders to establish or expand their operations in the city. HKSOA chairman Richard Hext said the measures reflected cooperation between the government, legislators and the shipping industry. “The shipping sector is a highly competitive industry, requiring the support of many community stakeholders, including the government and legislators,” Hext said. “The new tax measures are an excellent example of public-private partnership. Each and every such initiative adds to Hong Kong’s attraction as a global maritime capital.” The association, which represents more than 200 shipping and maritime-related businesses, said it would work with the Inland Revenue Department to help the industry adapt to the new requirements. Hong Kong has been offering preferential tax treatment to qualifying ship lessors since 2020, extending concessions to ship leasing managers and other commercial maritime service providers in subsequent years. The latest reforms form part of the government’s wider effort to strengthen the city’s role as a maritime finance, shipping and commodity trading centre. Petronas said the addition would provide greater flexibility in bringing gas resources to market and meeting regional and international demand. The company has been active in the LNG industry for more than four decades, with PFLNG TIGA representing another addition to its integrated LNG portfolio.

articles.body: Oil Falls as Supply Glut Concerns Overshadow Hormuz Shipping Risks Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 © Miha Creative / Adobe Stock Crude oil prices fell on Wednesday as the prospect of a market surplus offset concerns about disruptions to oil exports in the Middle East. Brent crude futures LCOc1 declined 44 cents, or 0.5%, to $90.96 a barrel at 1035 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures CLc1 slipped 62 cents, or 0.8%, to $81.43 a barrel. Both benchmarks gained more than 2% on Tuesday. "Investors are preoccupied with the thought of supply exceeding demand," said Tamas Varga, an oil analyst at PVM, a brokerage. On Wednesday, Yemen's Houthis said they had attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery ‌and Riyadh's financial district. Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, is part of a complex on the kingdom's Gulf coast ‌that ⁠also serves as a major export terminal for Saudi crude. A build-up in crude inventories is also contributing to the softer oil prices, Varga said. US crude stocks rose by 126,000 barrels in the week ended November 20, market sources said on Tuesday, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute. API/S Eight analysts polled by Reuters estimated that crude inventories rose by about 1.5 million barrels on average. "Uncertainty about OPEC's 2027 policies in the upcoming November 29 meeting, especially with the UAE no longer restricted by OPEC+ policies and Iraq seeking higher oil output capacity, as well as broader market risk-off are some reasons," said Zhenqiang Seto, a senior research specialist for oil at LSEG. OPEC+ ministers will hold a series of meetings on November 29 to decide on their 2027 output policy. "Since the release of an IEA report this month, perceptions of a global supply glut have kept prices in check," said Tsuyoshi Ueno, senior economist at NLI Research Institute. Attention is also focused on how next year's production quotas will be determined at the OPEC+ meeting, Ueno said. Iraq is pressing OPEC+ to lift its estimate of the country's crude oil production capacity, four people familiar with the matter said, heightening tensions over a review that will help determine how much members can pump next year. Libya's Sharara oil pipeline has also reopened after an "unlawful group" closed a valve on the pipeline, with oil beginning to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya. "However, attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz and exchanges of attacks between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis have raised uncertainty over the sustainability of this trend," Ueno said. A container ship was targeted and came to a stop on Tuesday while sailing an "unauthorised" route near the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said, according to state media. On Monday, three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles as they sailed east through the strait, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Tuesday. articles.body: Windcat Expands Offshore Fleet with Second Damen Multi-Purpose Vessel Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 (Credit: Windcat) Windcat has signed a contract with Damen Shipyards Group for a second Multi-Purpose Accommodation Support Vessel (MP-ASV) under its Innovation Series, expanding its planned fleet of vessels designed for offshore energy operations. The agreement, signed on November 24, follows Windcat's initial order in November 2025 for the first vessel in the series, which included an option for five additional units. The new MP-ASV design builds on the companies' earlier collaboration on the Elevation Series commissioning service operations vessels (CSOVs), incorporating additional capabilities for offshore wind, subsea cable repair, offshore accommodation and remotely operated vehicle (ROV) support. The vessels will measure 102 meters in length and 20 meters in width, with approximately 750 square meters of deck space and 111 cabins accommodating up to 190 personnel. Each MP-ASV will feature an offshore crane capable of operating as a 150-tonne subsea crane or a 15-tonne three-dimensional motion-compensated crane, alongside provisions for ROV installation. Personnel transfers will be supported by a 3D motion-compensated gangway with interchangeable tips designed for short connections in offshore wind operations and longer continuous connections. The vessels will also feature a DP2+ dynamic positioning system with DNV CBS and CBT class notations, incorporating additional bow and stern tunnel thrusters to improve redundancy during offshore operations. The propulsion and power arrangement will include a battery system for peak shaving, spinning reserve and electrical sailing, together with a dual-fuel hydrogen auxiliary generator. Three main generator sets supplied by ABC will feature its Evolve technology, designed to accommodate different fuel options, including biodiesel, hydrotreated vegetable oil (HVO), dual-fuel operation and gas. The MP-ASVs are designed for extended offshore deployments of up to 150 days, supported by increased fuel capacity and accommodation facilities intended for prolonged stays at sea. The Innovation Series builds on Damen and Windcat's Elevation Series partnership, which includes the Windcat Rotterdam, named KNVTS Ship of the Year at the 2026 Maritime Awards Gala.

articles.body: NextGeo Gets $12.7M Offshore Survey Job for Spain-France Hydrogen Link Maritime Activity Reports, Inc. November 25, 2026 Italian offshore services provider Next Geosolutions (NextGeo) has secured a contract worth approximately $12.7 million (€11.6 million) from BarMar for offshore survey work supporting the development of a planned hydrogen pipeline connecting Spain and France. The contract covers an integrated survey campaign along an approximately 366-kilometre offshore corridor between Barcelona, Spain, and Fos-sur-Mer, France. The scope includes geophysical, geotechnical and UXO surveys, grab sampling, remotely operated vehicle (ROV) inspections and surveys of crossings with existing subsea infrastructure. The data collected will be used to characterise seabed and sub-seabed conditions to support the planning and design of the future pipeline. NextGeo will deploy two dedicated vessels for the offshore operations, which are expected to begin by the end of 2026. The campaign is currently scheduled for completion between the end of the second quarter and the beginning of the third quarter of 2027, depending on any additional work requested during execution. The BarMar pipeline forms part of H2med, a cross-border initiative designed to connect hydrogen networks in the Iberian Peninsula with northwestern Europe. The project is being developed by BarMar S.A.S., whose shareholders are NaTran, Enagás and Teréga. H2med is included on the European Union's list of Projects of Common Interest, with BarMar providing the planned maritime hydrogen transport connection between Spain and France. The award marks NextGeo's first contract with BarMar, expanding its offshore survey activities into hydrogen infrastructure development.

articles.summary: Two established naval architecture and marine engineering firms become 100% employee owned, carrying forward the vision and values of their founders. Bristol Harbor Group, Inc. (BHGI) and The Shearer Group,...

Join the leading maritime news network Two established naval architecture and marine engineering firms become 100% employee owned, carrying forward the vision and values of their founders. Bristol Harbor Group, Inc. (BHGI) and The Shearer Group, Inc. (TSGI) are proud to announce that both companies are now 100% employee owned through an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), marking an important milestone for the two naval architecture and marine engineering firms. For Gregory W. Beers, P.E., and Cory C. Wood, who founded BHGI in 1995 and later established TSGI in 2010, the transition represents the continuation of a vision that began more than three decades ago: to build the most well-respected naval architecture and marine engineering firms in the industry. Gregory and Cory have spent decades building BHGI and TSGI with a vision that extends well beyond their own leadership. Through careful planning, the development of strong management teams, and a continued investment in their employees, they have positioned both firms to become multigenerational leaders in the naval architecture and marine engineering industry. The transition to employee ownership is a significant step in securing that future, ensuring that the companies they founded continue to grow and succeed for generations to come. While ownership has changed, both firms will continue operating much as they have for years. Gregory and Cory will remain at the forefront of both companies, providing leadership and direction alongside their established management teams. Clients can continue to expect the same level of service and technical expertise from the employees they’ve come to know and trust over the years. BHGI’s History BHGI traces its origins back to 1993, when Gregory and Cory, along with Andy Tyska of Bristol Marine and another fellow student at the University of Michigan Naval Architecture and Marine Engineering Department set out to design a passenger vessel while still in school. Their first design, the STAR OF SAUGATUCK II , marked an early milestone for the firm and is still operating on the Kalamazoo River in Southwest Michigan. Building on that early initiative, the group formally incorporated BHGI in 1995, and the firm has continued to grow in Bristol, Rhode Island, ever since. Over the years, BHGI has developed into a close-knit team of 19, maintaining a hands-on, collaborative working environment. Today, the engineering team is led by Daniel P. Eling, P.E. For more than three decades, BHGI has been guided by a set of core values established early on by Greg and Cory. Those values continue to shape the firm’s work today and center on technical excellence, attention to detail, a strong focus on clients, engineering ethics, professionalism, and responsibility. TSGI’s History In 2010, Gregory and Cory formed The Shearer Group, Inc. (TSGI), a sister company to BHGI located in Houston, Texas. The company was established when Gregory and Cory purchased the assets of Shearer & Assoc., Inc. from Edward L. Shearer, P.E., its founder and president. The three had heard of one another through industry connections and eventually met at a SNAME convention. That encounter led to further discussions, and ultimately the formation of TSGI. The “Shearer” name has long been associated with the inland marine industry, reflecting both Ed’s contributions to naval architecture and his family’s multigenerational barge line. When TSGI was established, it brought together Ed’s years of experience at Shearer & Associates, Inc. and the naval architecture and marine engineering expertise Gregory and Cory had developed at BHGI. Ed remains involved as a Principal Naval Architect. Today, TSGI provides marine engineering services to clients in the inland and offshore marine industries. The firm offers many of the same services as BHGI, along with additional services suited to its Houston location, including marine surveying and OSHA-compliant maritime gear certification support. As TSGI continued to grow, Joshua S. Sebastian, P.E., joined the firm in 2013, bringing five years of engineering experience at BHGI, along with his nine-year background as an officer in the U.S. Coast Guard. He relocated to Texas to serve as Engineering Manager, as part of Gregory and Cory’s plan to build TSGI with the same technical and cultural approach used at BHGI. In 2022, Joshua stepped into the role of Vice President – Operations, with Senior Naval Architect Harrison C. Brann, P.E., stepping into the role of Engineering Manager. Over 15 years, TSGI has grown into another close-knit team of 19. Under Joshua and Harrison’s leadership, TSGI has continued to grow while maintaining the same approach and core principles established at BHGI. Today, the firm remains dedicated to serving vessels that operate on the inland waterways and continuing the tradition established by its namesake. Leadership and Employee Ownership With the ESOP now in place, Gregory will serve as Chairman and President, Cory as Vice Chairman, and Joshua as Vice President of both BHGI and TSGI. The engineering teams will continue under the direction of Daniel at BHGI and Harrison at TSGI, both as Engineering Managers. What began as a design effort in a college house has grown into two established firms, each built in a steady and deliberate way. Over the years, Gregory and Cory have built management teams that allow BHGI and TSGI to grow without losing sight of the values on which they were founded. Now, with ownership in the hands of their employees, both firms will continue the work they were built to do, guided by the same commitment to their clients, their profession, and a shared belief that their purpose is to create. To mark the transition to employee ownership, BHGI and TSGI recognized employees who were with the firms at the time as “Plank Owners,” a nautical term traditionally used for members of a vessel’s commissioning crew. Each employee received a commemorative “Built to Last” challenge coin featuring the “Plank Owner” designation. Both offices also have permanent “Plank Owner” plaques on display, recognizing these employees and their place in the companies’ history. For BHGI and TSGI, employee ownership is another part of what it means to be built to last. About BHGI Bristol Harbor Group, Inc. (BHGI) is a naval architecture and marine engineering firm located in Bristol, Rhode Island. Founded in 1995, BHGI provides vessel design, engineering, and consulting services to commercial and government clients throughout the marine industry. To learn more, you can visit our website: http://bristolharborgroup.com . About TSGI The Shearer Group, Inc. (TSGI) is a naval architecture and marine engineering firm located in Houston, Texas. Established in 2010, TSGI provides naval architecture, marine engineering, marine surveying, and related consulting services to clients in the inland and offshore marine industries.
